summary: Describes an architecture for delay-tolerant and disruption-tolerant networks, evolved from the original design for the Interplanetary Internet, where links are long and often interrupted. This memo is informational.

eli5.summary: Space messages take minutes and links drop out. This design stores a message at each stop until the next link comes up, like passing a letter hand to hand.

how does dtn differ from tcp ip
subtitle: A store-and-forward overlay for networks where links are slow, intermittent or absent.

tldr.problem: Internet protocols assume a continuous end-to-end path, timely feedback and low loss, which fails in deep space, sensor, wireless, satellite and underwater networks.
tldr.mechanism: A message-oriented bundle layer above the transport layers moves variable-length bundles hop by hop, storing them in persistent storage until a contact is available, with optional custody transfer, priority classes and security.
tldr.outcome: It defines the architecture and its concepts, leaving the bundle format and security details to other documents. It is an IRTF consensus document, not a candidate for any Internet Standard.

sections.title: Why the Internet Model Falls Short
sections.content:
The architecture grew out of the Interplanetary Internet, but it targets any delay- and disruption-tolerant network (DTN). The RFC lists Internet assumptions that do not hold there: an end-to-end path exists for the whole session, retransmission based on timely feedback repairs errors, end-to-end loss is small, all routers support TCP/IP, and a single route is enough.

Its design principles answer these. Use variable-length messages instead of streams or small packets. Use a flexible naming syntax. Use storage inside the network, and do not require end-to-end reliability. Protect the infrastructure by discarding unauthorized traffic quickly. Offer coarse classes of service and a way to express data lifetime.

Other targets named include sensor networks with scheduled connectivity, wireless networks without end-to-end connectivity, satellite networks and underwater acoustic networks.
sections.eli5: The normal Internet expects a path to the other side to stay open and answers to come back quickly. Space and other tricky places cannot promise that, so this design plans for waiting.

sections.title: Bundles, Nodes and Endpoints
sections.content:
Applications send messages called ADUs (Application Data Units). The bundle layer, an overlay above the transport layers and below applications, turns them into bundles, which are the protocol data units. A bundle has two or more blocks. Bundles can be fragmented and reassembled anywhere in the network.

A DTN node implements the bundle layer. A DTN endpoint is a set of nodes, and delivery succeeds when a minimum reception group has received the bundle. An Endpoint Identifier (EID) names an endpoint using URI syntax, so many naming schemes fit. The RFC calls this late binding: a destination name may be reinterpreted at each hop instead of being resolved to an address at the source, as a DNS lookup does.

Unlike IP store-and-forward, where storing lasts roughly as long as queuing and transmission delay, DTN nodes may keep bundles for a long time, typically in persistent storage such as disk or flash that survives restarts.
sections.eli5: A big message is wrapped into a bundle, like a parcel with a label. Each stop reads the label and decides where to send it next, and keeps the parcel safe while it waits.

sections.title: Contacts, Routing and Fragmentation
sections.content:
A DTN is modeled as a time-varying multigraph. A period when an edge has positive capacity is a contact, and capacity times duration is its volume. Contact types are persistent, on-demand, scheduled, opportunistic and predicted. Known contacts allow smart routing, while uncertain ones make routing hard and remain an active research area.

Fragmentation helps use contact volumes fully. Proactive fragmentation splits data into smaller bundles up front and the final destination reassembles them. Reactive fragmentation happens when a transfer is cut short and the remainder is sent later, possibly to a different next hop. Reactive fragmentation is optional, partly because partial bundles break most message authentication codes, but reassembly at the destination is required.
sections.eli5: Some roads are open all the time, some only at set hours, and some show up by surprise. Big parcels can be split so that whatever fits through an open road goes now.

sections.title: Priorities, Custody and Reports
sections.content:
There are three relative priority classes: bulk, normal and expedited. They only order bundles from the same source. Applications may also pick delivery options such as custody transfer, a delivery report, an application acknowledgment, and diagnostic reports for reception, custody acceptance, forwarding and deletion.

With custody transfer, responsibility for reliable delivery moves between nodes called custodians, which acknowledge it with custody signals. The RFC compares it to a database commit. It is advisory and nodes need not accept it, so it is not a strict hop-by-hop mechanism. Without it, delivery depends on the underlying protocols.

Status reports and custody signals are administrative records, loosely like ICMP messages, but sent to the report-to EID or the current custodian instead of the source. Time synchronization is needed for bundle identification, scheduled routing, expiration and registration expiry. Flow and congestion control are left as unresolved research, and the authors state they have not reached full consensus on them.
sections.eli5: Like postal mail, you can choose fast or slow service, ask for a receipt, or ask a trusted stop to take responsibility for the parcel. Stops can say no if they are too full.

sections.title: Security, State and Applications
sections.content:
Security is optional but integral. Because storage and links can be scarce, nodes should discard unauthorized or damaged traffic as early as possible. The architecture uses hop-by-hop and end-to-end authentication and integrity, with details in separate documents. The cost is extra computation and credential storage. Revoking credentials is especially hard when connectivity is poor.

The RFC also lists state a node keeps: application registrations, custody transfer state, routing and forwarding information, security material and policy. Convergence layers adapt the bundle layer to each underlying protocol, so a TCP one may only add message boundaries.

Applications must be delay tolerant too. They should pack enough information into each ADU to minimize round trips, and survive restarts while replies are pending. The RFC says a bundled file request can finish in one round trip, where an FTP put can need as many as eight.
sections.eli5: Guards at each stop turn away fake parcels right away. Programs should also put everything in one parcel instead of chatting back and forth, since each reply can take ages.

items.label: Least effort
items.desc: Shipped only after other classes for the same source and destination.

items.label: Expedited
items.desc: Generally shipped before bundles of other classes.
